description: nf-core/eager TSV samplesheet context, aligned to the pinned 2.5.3 schema (a DSL1 release, run with Nextflow 22.10.8). Ancient DNA: damage-aware mapping, deduplication, damage profiles, authentication, contamination, genetic sex and genotyping.

mapper.help: bwaaln for short, damaged ancient reads (upstream's default, eager's recommended aDNA mapper); bwamem when the libraries hold mostly long reads (well-preserved or modern controls); circularmapper when the question is about a circular genome (mitochondria, a bacterial chromosome) and reads spanning its origin must map; bowtie2 when a study's protocol names it.

dedupper.help: dedup when every library is paired-end and its reads are merged (it uses both ends of a molecule, so set mergedonly with it); markduplicates when any library is single-end or the cohort mixes single- and paired-end data (eager's usage.md advises it then).

mergedonly.help: true with dedupper dedup, or when the question needs only reads whose mates overlapped (short ancient molecules): unmerged pairs and singletons are dropped after AdapterRemoval.

complexity_filter_poly_g.help: true when any library was sequenced on a 2-colour instrument (NextSeq, NovaSeq; Colour_Chemistry 2): fastp trims the poly-G tails those instruments write on short molecules. It acts only on Colour_Chemistry 2 rows.

run_bam_filtering.help: true when the question needs only confidently placed or long-enough reads (genotyping, population genetics) or a minimum mapping quality; required for bam_mapping_quality_threshold and bam_filter_minreadlength.

bam_mapping_quality_threshold.help: minimum mapping quality kept after mapping, when run_bam_filtering is on and the question needs uniquely placed reads (25 to 30 is common for human population genetics); 0 keeps every mapped read.

bam_filter_minreadlength.help: minimum read length kept after mapping, when run_bam_filtering is on and very short spurious hits must go (often 30 to 35 for aDNA); 0 keeps every length.

damage_calculation_tool.help: how C-to-T damage at read ends is measured, the first authentication evidence for ancient DNA: damageprofiler (upstream's default), or mapdamage when the study compares with earlier mapDamage results.

run_pmdtools.help: true when the question needs reads authenticated as ancient one by one (a sample with modern contamination): PMDtools scores each read's post-mortem damage and keeps reads at or above pmdtools_threshold.

pmdtools_threshold.help: PMD score a read needs to be kept by run_pmdtools; raise it when the question needs stricter authentication at the cost of reads.

run_trim_bam.help: true for non-UDG or half-UDG libraries going into genotyping: damaged bases at read ends are clipped by the bamutils_clip_* lengths. eager applies it only to UDG_Treatment none or half rows.

bamutils_clip_double_stranded_half_udg_l.help: bases clipped from the 5' end of double-stranded half-UDG reads with run_trim_bam, from the damage profile (half-UDG damage stays in the first one or two bases).

bamutils_clip_double_stranded_half_udg_r.help: bases clipped from the 3' end of double-stranded half-UDG reads with run_trim_bam, from the damage profile.

bamutils_clip_double_stranded_none_udg_l.help: bases clipped from the 5' end of double-stranded non-UDG reads with run_trim_bam, as far as the damage profile shows elevated C-to-T.

bamutils_clip_double_stranded_none_udg_r.help: bases clipped from the 3' end of double-stranded non-UDG reads with run_trim_bam, as far as the damage profile shows elevated G-to-A.

bamutils_clip_single_stranded_half_udg_l.help: bases clipped from the 5' end of single-stranded half-UDG reads with run_trim_bam, from the damage profile.

bamutils_clip_single_stranded_half_udg_r.help: bases clipped from the 3' end of single-stranded half-UDG reads with run_trim_bam, from the damage profile.

bamutils_clip_single_stranded_none_udg_l.help: bases clipped from the 5' end of single-stranded non-UDG reads with run_trim_bam, from the damage profile.

bamutils_clip_single_stranded_none_udg_r.help: bases clipped from the 3' end of single-stranded non-UDG reads with run_trim_bam, from the damage profile.

run_genotyping.help: true when the question asks for genotypes or variants (population genetics, a pathogen's SNPs, a consensus); needs genotyping_tool.

genotyping_tool.help: the genotyper run_genotyping uses: ug (GATK 3.5 UnifiedGenotyper, eager's advice for low-coverage aDNA), hc (GATK4 HaplotypeCaller, for higher coverage) or freebayes (haploid or pooled data). pileupcaller and angsd are not offered: pileupcaller needs a SNP panel not staged on Luria, and angsd writes genotype likelihoods, not a VCF reingest can register.

genotyping_source.help: which BAM is genotyped: raw (deduplicated), trimmed (needs run_trim_bam; for non- or half-UDG libraries, so damage does not become false SNPs) or pmd (needs run_pmdtools; only damage-authenticated reads).

gatk_call_conf.help: phred-scaled confidence a GATK call needs; lower it only when the question accepts more false calls for more sites at low coverage.

gatk_ploidy.help: ploidy GATK genotypes with, from the organism: 2 for human or animal nuclear DNA, 1 for a haploid pathogen or a mitochondrial genome.

freebayes_p.help: ploidy FreeBayes genotypes with, from the organism: 2 for diploid nuclear DNA, 1 for a haploid pathogen.

run_sexdeterrmine.help: true when the question asks the genetic sex of human individuals (human reference only): relative X and Y coverage per library.

run_nuclear_contamination.help: true when the question asks how contaminated human male samples are (ANGSD's X-chromosome method; human reference only).

contamination_chrom_name.help: the X chromosome's name in the reference, for run_nuclear_contamination: chrX for the GENCODE GRCh38 FASTA staged on Luria, X for an Ensembl or hs37d5 reference.

run_mtnucratio.help: true when the question compares mitochondrial with nuclear DNA content (preservation, or whether a library is mostly mtDNA).

mtnucratio_header.help: the mitochondrial contig's name in the reference, for run_mtnucratio: chrM for the GENCODE GRCh38 and GRCm39 FASTAs staged on Luria, MT for the Ensembl macaque references.

snpcapture_bed.help: for SNP-capture libraries (1240K and similar), the panel's BED as a path on the cluster, so coverage is reported on the targets; ask the user when the libraries' metadata says capture.

save_reference.help: true when later runs on the same reference should reuse the BWA index, FASTA index and dictionary this run builds (they are written to reference_genome/).

pipeline.name: nf-core/eager
pipeline.core_rule: One row per library and lane, tab-separated, with exactly the eleven columns Sample_Name, Library_ID, Lane, Colour_Chemistry, SeqType, Organism, Strandedness, UDG_Treatment, R1, R2, BAM, every cell filled (NA where unused). eager reads --input as a TSV only when its name ends in .tsv.

validation_rules: The file is tab-separated and named samplesheet.tsv, with exactly the eleven columns in order; any other column, or a row with a different number of fields, stops eager.

Write each row with the generic names sample, fastq_1 and fastq_2: the emitter renames them to Sample_Name, R1 and R2, fills SeqType (PE or SE) from the reads it finds, Library_ID from the sample when blank, and NA into an empty R2, BAM or Organism.

Colour_Chemistry (2 or 4), Strandedness (single or double) and UDG_Treatment (none, half or full) come from the param atlas verdicts for each sample; when a verdict is absent or a conflict the user is asked. Never guess UDG treatment: it changes how damage is handled.
Lane is the L00N number from the file name when present, else 1; it must differ between rows of one library.
Every sample needs its FASTQ on the cluster: a TSV sheet cannot be filled by the archive download, so a sample with no local reads is refused.

run_genotyping needs genotyping_tool; genotyping_source trimmed needs run_trim_bam and pmd needs run_pmdtools; bam_mapping_quality_threshold needs run_bam_filtering. configure_run refuses these combinations, as eager would mid-run.
The metagenomic screen (MALT or Kraken2, and MaltExtract authentication) is not offered: its classifier databases are not staged on Luria. Say so when the question asks for one.
run_sexdeterrmine and run_nuclear_contamination are for human references only.
notes: eager 2.5.3 is DSL1, so its run.sh launches it as NXF_VER=22.10.8 nextflow run (the catalog's nextflow_version); that release, its Java and the DSL1 run on Luria are UNVERIFIED. The reference is the species' FASTA staged under refs/ (GENCODE GRCh38 for human, whose contigs are chr-prefixed); eager builds its BWA index from it on every run unless save_reference keeps it. No MALT or Kraken2 database, SNP panel (pileupCaller, sexdeterrmine error bars) or dbSNP is staged.

samplesheet_columns.description: Column-level field dictionary for the nf-core/eager input TSV (main.nf extract_data at 2.5.3).

Sample_Name.description: Sample; its libraries are merged after deduplication.
Sample_Name.validation_hints: The NExtSEEK D.SEQ UID, written as `sample`.

Library_ID.description: Library; its lanes are merged after clipping. Must be unique across samples.
Library_ID.validation_hints: Left blank, the emitter writes the sample UID (one library per D.SEQ).

Lane.description: Lane the library was sequenced on.
Lane.validation_hints: The L00N token from the file name, else 1.

Colour_Chemistry.description: 2 for NextSeq or NovaSeq, 4 for HiSeq or MiSeq; decides poly-G trimming.
Colour_Chemistry.validation_hints: From the param atlas verdict (the D.SEQ Sequencer); 4 when the metadata names no instrument.

SeqType.validation_hints: Filled by the emitter from the reads it finds.

Organism.description: Organism name; unused by eager, but it splits merging when it differs.
Organism.validation_hints: The species with no spaces (Homo_sapiens), or blank for NA.

Strandedness.validation_hints: From the param atlas verdict (the library's LibraryType and Protocol); double when they say nothing. Not the D.SEQ Strandedness field, which is RNA-seq's.

UDG_Treatment.description: UDG (USER) treatment of the library; decides damage trimming and genotyping caveats.
UDG_Treatment.validation_hints: From the param atlas verdict; asked when the metadata does not say.

R1.validation_hints: Written as fastq_1; the emitter fills it from the sample's Link_PrimaryData or File_PrimaryData.

R2.validation_hints: Written as fastq_2; NA when the sample has one read file.

BAM.description: BAM input; NA for FASTQ input, the only input offered here.

report_writer_guidance.purpose: Build an nf-core/eager TSV from a resolved NExtSEEK D.SEQ cohort of ancient DNA libraries.
report_writer_guidance.workflow_role: Selected for ancient DNA (damage, authentication, contamination, sex, genotyping). Modern DNA variant calling is sarek's.
report_writer_guidance.output_expectation: TSV with header Sample_Name, Library_ID, Lane, Colour_Chemistry, SeqType, Organism, Strandedness, UDG_Treatment, R1, R2, BAM.
population_priority: One row per D.SEQ: sample = the UID; Lane from the file name.
Colour_Chemistry, Strandedness and UDG_Treatment from each sample's data_driven_params verdict.
Say plainly that no metagenomic screen runs and why.
final_checks: Exactly eleven tab-separated columns, every cell filled.
No two rows share Library_ID + Lane.

runtime.basis: First guess for one 16-CPU Luria node (Nessie's default submit); not yet measured on Luria. Shotgun aDNA libraries are small; capture libraries smaller. Refine from real runs.
runtime.setup_label: first run on a reference builds its BWA index
